memory_candidates.content: When adding bounded retry on top of a function that already holds a process-global mutex for its ENTIRE body (acquired at entry, released via a RETURN trap), never place the retry loop inside that function. Instead write an outer wrapper that calls the original function fresh, in full, per attempt -- the mutex is then acquired and released once per attempt rather than held across the whole wait window, which would otherwise block every other concurrent caller system-wide and risk the mutex being reclaimed by a competing waiter after its staleness threshold. This also automatically preserves any same-identity/re-entry fast-path inside the wrapped function, since every attempt re-runs that check from scratch.

A collision-detection predicate built on a periodic state.json STATUS read (rather than a live lock scan) only clears once the colliding entity reaches a genuinely TERMINAL status. A resequencing/retry mechanism layered on top of such a predicate will only converge if the interfering work's natural completion actually transitions it to that terminal status within the retry window -- if the natural terminus is a non-terminal intermediate status, the retry will structurally never converge and must gracefully degrade to a bounded-give-up outcome rather than assuming convergence is guaranteed. Always check what the underlying predicate actually keys on (lock existence vs. status field) before assuming a second attempt will succeed.

git-commit-scoped.sh (and a bare `git add`) treats a trailing-slash task-directory pathspec as failing when the directory contains gitignored dotfiles/subdirectories, even when explicit `:(exclude)...` pathspecs are also passed for those exact paths -- git still emits its ignored-paths warning and returns a non-zero exit for the whole `git add` invocation, which the wrapper script (correctly, defensively) treats as a hard failure and aborts the commit. Workaround: pass explicit file paths instead of the trailing-slash directory (e.g. list `plans/01_x.md`, `.return-meta.json` individually rather than `specs/NNN_slug/`) to avoid git's directory-recursion-into-ignored-paths warning entirely.
